# The challenge: training DRCs {.smaller .center}

:::::: columns
:::: {.column width="60%"}

We are seeing a **computational turn in research**, as seen in a


-   growing number of research that relies on **data** or **research software** [@crouch2013],

-   adoption of **computational methods** by fields that didn't traditionally use them (e.g. computational social sciences, digital humanities...)

-   growing importance of **OpenScience** and expectation to manage data and outputs following **FAIR principles**,

-   growing number of infrastructure and professionals needed for its delivery,

-   the advent of AI (adding a new level of complexity).

This **requires a broad set of skills -[Digital Research Competencies]{.highlight-text} [(DRC)]{.highlight-text}-** that need to be [learnt]{.highlight-text} and [taught]{.highlight-text}.
::::

::: {.column width="40%"}
![[DIRECT Framework](https://directframework.com/) [@nenadic2026]](/media/DIRECT%20Framework_alpha.png)
:::
::::::

::: notes

This requires a broad set skills -Digital Research Competencies- that need to be learnt and taught.

DIRECT framework acknowledges the importance and diversity of training and Digital Research Competencies, but it does not explain some of the questions that we were having...

:::

# So we wondered...

::::: columns
::: {.column width="60%"}
-   If training is needed, and RSEs are not doing it, [who are the professionals filling this gap]{.highlight-text}?

-   If multiple professionals are doing it: [does the]{.highlight-text} [training differ based on their backgrounds?]{.highlight-text}

-   And more broadly: how are DRC being delivered and what are their [key defining]{.highlight-text} [factors]{.highlight-text}?
:::

# Our research {.smaller background-color="#DAD6CA"}

***"Mapping and evaluating dRTP’s contributions to computing skills and pedagogies in Higher Education"*** **is a project funded by the UKRI's [DisCouRSE Network+](https://discourse-network.github.io/) and [aims to map and analyse the provision of digital research]{.highlight-text} [competencies (DRC)]{.highlight-text} which are led by or involve dRTP’s across Higher Education institutions in the UK.**

::::: {.columns .smaller}
::: {.column width="70%"}
The research acknowledges and complements existing competency frameworks like DIRECT but examines the material conditions of training delivery instead on learning needs.

Research questions include:

-   How are dRTPs engaging in the teaching of Digital Research Competencies?

-   What are the methodologies and technologies used to deliver the training? How are decisions on training delivery made?

-   How is the training influenced by matters such as type of professional, career stage, background, pedagogical approaches, trends, availability, licences or teachers’ beliefs?

-   Are there any approaches that are more frequently used for specific audiences or cases?
:::

::: {.column width="30%"}
![](/media/DisCouRSE-Logo-Light.svg){width="400"} [This work was supported by the [DisCouRSE Network+](https://discourse-network.github.io/), which received funding through the UKRI Digital Research Infrastructure Programme]{.caption}
:::
:::::

::: notes

# Methodology

## Survey {.smaller}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="70%"}
**People**

-   Who are involved? What are their job titles?

-   How are they involved in the teaching?

-   Do they have any [pedagogical background]{.highlight-text}?

-   What are their [beliefs]{.highlight-text} in relation to tech and pedagogy? *(e.g. stance as a teacher, importance of opensource, AI, licences...)*

**Training and pedagogies**

-   What is being taught?

-   What [formats]{.highlight-text} and [delivery mode]{.highlight-text} are used?

-   What are the [key factors]{.highlight-text} influencing how the training is delivered?

-   Infrastructure needed

-   Challenges
:::

::: {.column width="30%"}
![Link to the survey: <https://tinyurl.com/DRTP-training-survey>](media/qualtrics-qrcode.png)
:::
